solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Future foreign secretaries excited by the thrill of the chase?

definitions.text: Future foreign secretaries excited by the thrill of the chase?

parts.words: Future foreign secretaries excited by the thrill of the chase?
parts.note: people who come after Jeremy Hunt as Foreign Secretary follow Hunt; riders keen on chasing foxes follow the hunt

explanation.surface: A sneer at ambitious politicians who love the scent of power as huntsmen love the chase.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt was the UK Foreign Secretary when this appeared, so his successors are, punningly, his followers. Foxhunting is a traditional British country sport with riders following the hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who ride along with a foxhunt are called its followers, and Jeremy Hunt's successors in office also come after him.

clue.text: Tool hits a wife on the bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry the last piece sits at the foot of the column, below the rest

parts.note: to hack is to strike or chop roughly

explanation.surface: A violent picture of someone striking a spouse on the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, an example of a tool.

clue.text: Edit blooper in new medium? Easy peasy!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothes sizes

indicators.note: editing a blooper reworks it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcaster shrugging off the job of cutting an outtake for a new platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edit' reads as a broadcaster's chore but is the rearranging signal, and 'in' sets the jumbled letters between the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual exclamations saying a task is simple and no trouble at all.

clue.text: New profits-led society organised shooting and fishing etc

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the letters of the hyphenated phrase take a new order

explanation.surface: A newly formed money-driven club arranging country pursuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PROFITSLED into FIELDSPORT; 'organised' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting, shooting and fishing are the classic outdoor country pursuits grouped under this collective name.

clue.text: Sluggish (unlike Ko-Ko)

definitions.meaning: Ko-Ko, the Lord High Executioner in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, sings that he has a little list, so someone unlike him has none

explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan; Ko-Ko's list is of people who would not be missed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking energy is the ordinary sense; read in two parts it also means having no list, which Ko-Ko has.

clue.text: Circulates gold coins

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
bits are small coins, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A report that gold coins are in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round and round something in a path is a synonym of circling it.

clue.text: UK decried broken down supplier

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled in a different order

explanation.surface: The country condemned a feather merchant that went bust.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea bird's soft breast feathers are collected to fill quilts, so it provides the stuffing.

clue.text: Glasses picking up tiny bits of dust?

indicators.note: picking up a signal is hearing it, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: specks are tiny particles

explanation.surface: Spectacles gathering motes of dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of spectacles is informally shortened to this word.

clue.text: See 3
Tree common to Bar-le-Duc, Ypres, Somme

indicators.note: the letters are shared across the end of one place name and the start of the next ones

explanation.surface: A tree found in all three northern French First World War towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar-le-Duc, Ypres and the Somme are battle-scarred places of the Western Front.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall evergreen conifer is a kind of tree, often planted in cemeteries.

clue.text: Move Chancellor's speech — time's at an end

indicators.note: read as 'is', saying time is up: the letter for time gives way to the word for finished

parts.note: the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer presents the Budget to Parliament
up means over, as in time's up

explanation.surface: A tired MP urging the Chancellor to move it along as the speech runs over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time's at an end' is read as 'T's up', so T at the end of BUDGET is swapped for UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to shift along a seat to make room uses this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Normandy beach where Yankee drops off, sleepy in retirement

indicators.note: dropping off means falling away, so that letter leaves
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: drowsy means sleepy
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American nods off on a Normandy beach while sleepily retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' turns DROWSY into YSWORD; 'drops off' removes Y.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five D-Day landing beaches in Normandy, assigned to British forces, was codenamed so.

clue.text: Scold Ms Minelli; Spooner says she spends half the day in bed

definitions.text: she spends half the day in bed

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: to rate someone is to scold them
Liza Minelli, the singer and actress

explanation.surface: A telling-off for Liza Minelli for lying in bed until noon.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of RATE LIZA gives LATE RIZA, said as the answer in non-rhotic speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets up late, lazing in bed half the morning, is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Woman garlanded with Oscar vacating set location for Stagecoach?

indicators.note: a garland wraps round, so the writer's name surrounds the single letter

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish writer and wit

indicators.note: vacating means emptying, so the word loses its insides and keeps its outer letters

explanation.surface: A film actress wreathed with an Academy Award, leaving the film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the film award but is Oscar Wilde. Stagecoach is the 1939 John Ford Western.
explanation.definitionFit: The frontier of the 19th-century American West is where the classic Western film is set.

clue.text: Turns to listen to explanation for turbulence

parts.note: winds means turns or twists
to hear is to listen

explanation.surface: An aviation instruction to turn and pay attention to the reason for a bumpy flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden change in wind speed or direction over a short distance is a common cause of air turbulence.

clue.text: They try following Joshua

definitions.meaning: people who try cases in court
the Old Testament book that comes after the Book of Joshua

explanation.definitionFit: Court officials who hear cases bear this name, which is also the title of the seventh book of the Bible.

clue.text: Georgia left underwear on in Texan resort

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a vest is an undershirt in British English

explanation.surface: A tourist from Georgia leaves underwear on at a Texas holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is worn under a shirt, not over it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf Coast island city in Texas is a well-known beach destination.

clue.text: Liberal Dem Cable in the doldrums

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are given free arrangement

explanation.surface: Vince Cable, Liberal Democrat leader, stuck going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks part of the party name but signals the rearrangement. Vince Cable led the UK Liberal Democrats at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing ship stalled for lack of wind in the equatorial calms is stuck motionless, the sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Arab chaps visiting the old island

indicators.note: visitors go inside a place, so the chaps go in between the other two pieces

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Arab men calling on an ancient island.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Yemen, on the Arabian Peninsula, is an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: Court jester's run away? Come on you dogs; after him!

definitions.text: Come on you dogs; after him!

indicators.note: run away means the letter for run goes

parts.note: Yorick was the king's jester in Hamlet, his skull dug up by the gravedigger
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jester flees the court, with hounds set on his trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away' looks like the jester bolting; it removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional foxhunting cry urging the hounds on, used as an exclamation of excitement.

clue.text: Angela blows her top, getting live coverage; it's the end of Jeremy Hunt

indicators.note: being covered means being enclosed, so the shortened surname goes inside

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: her top letter goes, as if blown off

parts.note: Angela Merkel, the German Chancellor

indicators.note: the final letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: Merkel loses her temper on live television, spelling the end of Jeremy Hunt's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' looks to belong with Jeremy, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gloucestershire foxhunt is among the oldest packs of hounds in England, an example of a hunt.

clue.text: New York's north-eastern suburb?

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters form something fresh

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A question about a commuter town to the north-east of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' looks to be one name; 'New' is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This city lies just north of the Bronx, in effect a suburb of the city of New York.

clue.text: Where's Palin broadcast? I'll inquire of that lady

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air

parts.note: I'll ask her, said quickly

explanation.surface: A journalist asks after Sarah Palin and offers to question her directly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Palin was governor of this US state. The sound match relies on non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Palin was this US state's governor, so it is where she comes from.

clue.text: Actor tucking into squid risotto and mussel basmati

indicators.note: the actor is tucked inside the first dish, so its outer letters fall away to leave the first name
and carries the same tucking-into instruction on to the second dish, whose outer letters go to leave the surname

explanation.surface: A film star enjoying a seafood and rice dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first name hides in 'squid risotto' and the surname in 'mussel basmati'.
explanation.definitionFit: This British star of Luther and The Wire is an example of an actor.

clue.text: Switzerland supports managed agricultural land

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Swiss backing for a managed farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A large farm for raising cattle or other livestock is agricultural land.

clue.text: Maintain quills, with which to write note (enclosed)

indicators.note: the bracketed word is placed inside the writing tool

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions for keeping quill pens in order and writing a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quills' looks like writing pens, but they are a bird's feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird tends its feathers with its beak, the sense of grooming.

clue.text: Applaud Thom, regularly walking Mickey's dog

indicators.note: every other letter, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Praise for Thom, a dog walker taking out Mickey Mouse's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Mouse's pet in Disney cartoons is a bloodhound named this.

clue.text: Livingstone's taking McCluskey round refuge in Battersea

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, the former Mayor of London

indicators.note: turning round means going backwards

parts.note: Len McCluskey, the trade union leader

explanation.surface: Ken Livingstone bringing Len McCluskey round to a shelter in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs Home is a famous London animal shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs are housed and boarded in such places, as at the famous Battersea home for strays.

clue.text: Montana to release cop from over the border

parts.note: the setter took MO for Montana, though that is Missouri's abbreviation (Montana is MT)
to untie is to release

explanation.surface: Montana letting go a police officer from Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter slipped: MO is Missouri, not Montana, and later apologised.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is a police officer from north of the US border.

clue.text: Where to get a quick one followed by a few chasers?

definitions.text: Where to get a quick one followed by a few chasers?

parts.note: a hare is a swift animal
and links what comes after
hounds chase their quarry

explanation.surface: A drinker looking for a pub for a quick drink and some chasers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick one' and 'chasers' look like drinks; they are the hare and the pursuing hounds. The answer is a common English pub name and a paper-chase game.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional pub name, so somewhere a quick drink and chasers can be had.
